historical_record.description: The Glide Foundation established the Glide Urban Center here in 1962, a community organising centre operating out of Glide Memorial Church; it later housed the offices and symposia of the Council on Religion and the Homosexual.

Glide Memorial United Methodist Church is listed individually on the National Register of Historic Places for its social history, African American and Asian American heritage and its architecture, and is a contributing building in a district. Identified in 2024 as eligible for city landmark designation as well.

Glide Memorial Methodist Church helped create the Council on Religion and the Homosexual in 1964, after opening a dialogue with the city's homosexual activists about the young hustlers of the Tenderloin. The Council devoted itself to combating homophobia inside mainline churches.
Glide Memorial Methodist Church hosted a conference on alternatives to the draft, one of several counterculture-era events and services the church was associated with.
